rw: Extracurricular activities are optional programs such as clubs, sports and student groups that take place outside regular classes, which lets students build skills and interests beyond the standard curriculum and grades.

ww.Homework assignments that students do at: Homework is coursework that students complete at home as part of their regular classes, so it is not an activity held outside the normal class program like a club or team.
ww.Exams taken at school at the end of each: Exams are tests given at school as part of regular classes and grading, so they are academic requirements and not optional activities such as clubs or sports teams outside class.
ww.Required classes that all students must: Required classes are courses every student must take as part of the standard curriculum, which makes them regular instruction and not activities that students choose to join outside the school day.

rw: FBLA is a student business organization, and members build business skills, leadership experience and professional contacts that help when they plan a career and apply for jobs after school.

ww.They avoid all competition between membe: FBLA actually runs competitive events between members and chapters, so saying it avoids all competition is false, and competing is one of the main ways members build business skills.
ww.They replace the need for school and for: A club cannot replace school or classes, since members still attend them; FBLA adds experience to schooling and does not stand in for the education that careers require.
ww.They guarantee a job after graduation wi: No club can guarantee a job after graduation, because employers make their own hiring choices; FBLA only improves a member's skills and contacts, which raises the chances of getting hired.

rw: Job boards, company websites and personal contacts are the main places where openings are posted or heard about, so using all three gives a job seeker the widest chance of finding real openings.

ww.A job that pays the most money in a larg: This describes a kind of job a person might want, not a place to look, so it tells you nothing about where job openings are actually posted or advertised to applicants.
ww.A job at the top of a company with a big: A job at the top of a company with a large staff is a type of position, not a source of listings, so it does not say where to find openings.
ww.Nowhere, since jobs are secret and fille: Jobs are publicly advertised on boards, company sites and through contacts, and many openings are never secret, so claiming that no one can find them is false and discourages a real search.

rw: A resume summarizes who you are for an employer, so it lists contact details, education, skills and work experience, which together let the reader judge whether you fit the job quickly.

ww.Your friends' names and their phone numb: Friends' names and phone numbers do not belong on a resume, because an employer wants your own qualifications; only chosen references with permission may be listed on a separate page.
ww.Your passwords and your bank account num: Passwords and bank account numbers are private and must never appear on a resume, since sharing them could lead to fraud or identity theft and they say nothing about job qualifications.
ww.Your favorite foods and your favorite sh: Favorite foods and shows are personal interests that do not show job qualifications, so they waste space on a resume that should focus on education, skills and experience relevant to the work.

rw: School activities, volunteering and relevant skills show responsibility, teamwork and ability, so they fill a resume well for a student who has not held a paid job yet.

ww.A list of games played, with scores and: A list of games played with scores and teams does not show workplace skills, so it adds little value; relevant school activities, volunteering and skills give a stronger picture of what a student offers.
ww.Nothing at all, as you have no skills to: Having no work experience does not mean having no skills, since schoolwork, activities and volunteering build real abilities; leaving the resume empty would make the applicant look unprepared and uninterested.
ww.Made-up jobs that you never held at any: Inventing jobs never held is dishonest, and employers check references and records, so a false entry can cost the applicant the job offer and damage their reputation badly.

rw: Tailoring highlights the skills and experience the employer asks for in the posting, which shows you match what the employer needs and makes your application stand out from the others received.

ww.To avoid proofreading your own work late: Tailoring a resume takes extra effort and does not remove the need to proofread; careful checking is still required, so this reason gets the purpose of tailoring backward.
ww.To hide your experience from employers: Hiding experience would hurt your chances, because tailoring means highlighting the experience that matches the job, so employers see more relevant strengths and not fewer of them.
ww.To make it longer than a single page: Length is not the goal, and most resumes for entry-level jobs should fit on one page, so tailoring focuses on relevance and does not try to stretch the document.

rw: Proofreading means carefully reading finished writing to find and fix mistakes in spelling, grammar and punctuation, which keeps a resume or letter looking professional and free of errors before sending.

ww.Sending a document by email to a client: Sending a document by email is just delivering it and involves no review of the writing, so this describes transmission and not the careful checking that proofreading means.
ww.Writing a draft quickly in one sitting: Writing a quick draft in one sitting is drafting, which comes before proofreading; proofreading happens later, once the writing exists and needs checking for errors before it goes out.
ww.Printing a document on paper for use: Printing a document puts it on paper and does not check the content, so a printed resume can still hold mistakes that only careful proofreading would catch and correct beforehand.

rw: An address built from your own name looks professional and is easy for an employer to recognize, remember and match to the name on your resume and application materials.

map.Choosing a job because a friend likes it: A joke phrase from a game

ww.A funny nickname or slang: A funny nickname or slang in an address looks unprofessional, and employers may judge the applicant as not serious, so it should be saved for personal use and not job applications.
ww.A joke phrase from a game: A joke phrase from a game looks careless to an employer reading a job application, and it does not identify you by name, which makes it a poor choice.
ww.A random string of symbols: A random string of symbols is hard to read, type and remember, and it does not identify you, so employers may mistype it or doubt that you are professional.

map.A form for filing taxes with the state e: Nothing happens because employers never check social media
map.A record of your spending kept in a note: The employer will give you a bonus for being so honest in public
map.It will help you stand out positively in: It will make you stand out in a positive way to the employer

rt: The employer may doubt your judgment and reject your application
rw: Hiring managers often review public profiles, and a rude post can make them doubt your judgment and professionalism, so you may lose the job offer even if your resume is strong.

ww.Nothing happens because employers never: Nothing happens because employers never check social media is false, since many hiring managers review public profiles and may rethink an applicant after seeing a rude post.
ww.The employer will give you a bonus for b: An employer will not pay a bonus for being so honest online, since a rude public post reflects poor judgment and is more likely to cost you the job.
ww.It will make you stand out in a positive: A rude public post will not help you stand out positively, since employers look for good judgment and respect, and a negative post usually hurts an application and harms your reputation.

map.Accurate contact details such as an emai: A friend to answer the questions for you

map.Nothing at all: Nothing at all, since nothing is needed

rt: Extra copies of your resume and references
rw: Extra copies of your resume and references let the interviewers read about your background and contact your references, which shows you are prepared and organized for the meeting at hand.

ww.A friend to answer the questions for you: A friend answering for you shows you cannot speak for yourself, and interviewers want to hear from the candidate directly, so bringing a friend to answer questions would hurt your chances.
ww.Your lunch to eat during the interview: Eating your own lunch during an interview is unprofessional and distracting, so food should not be brought into the room, and it does nothing to show your qualifications.
ww.Nothing at all, since nothing is needed: Arriving with nothing at all is poor preparation, because you would have no resume copies or reference list to give the interviewer and would look unready for the position.

rw: STAR stands for Situation, Task, Action and Result, which gives a clear structure for telling a story about a past experience and showing the skills the employer wants to see.

ww.Skills, Training, Aims, Rewards: Skills, Training, Aims and Rewards is not what STAR stands for, and it gives no structure for telling a story about a past experience during an interview answer.
ww.Salary, Title, Hours, Benefits: Salary, Title, Hours and Benefits are job offer details to discuss, not the meaning of STAR, which is a way of organizing answers about your past experience.
ww.Speak, Think, Answer, Relax: Speak, Think, Answer and Relax is invented advice and not the STAR method; STAR uses Situation, Task, Action and Result to structure a story about what you did.

map.A tax return filed with the state each y: Recite your whole work history from the first job onward
map.A contract that guarantees a job to the: Say you have never had a problem and change the subject
map.A bill from the employer for the use of: Blame a former coworker and avoid describing your own role

rw: STAR means describing the situation, your task, the action you took and the result, which turns a question about solving a problem into a clear and complete example for the interviewer.

ww.Recite your whole work history from the: Reciting your whole work history does not answer a question about one problem, and it ignores STAR, which asks for a focused story with a situation, task, action and result.
ww.Say you have never had a problem and cha: Saying you never had a problem and changing the subject avoids the question, and it gives the interviewer no example of your skills, which is exactly what STAR is meant to supply.
ww.Blame a former coworker and avoid descri: Blaming a former coworker leaves out your own task and action and shows poor attitude, so it fails STAR, which asks you to describe what you did and the result.

rw: A follow-up email thanks the interviewer and reminds the employer of your interest and fit, which keeps you in mind while the hiring decision is still being made.

map.A job offer letter sent to a new hire by: A complaint to the employer about the interview questions
map.A copy of your diploma from a school or: A request that the employer forward your resume to others
map.A list of your hobbies and interests out: A long list of your hobbies and interests outside of work

ww.A complaint to the employer about the in: A complaint about the interview questions would make you look negative and hurt your chances, and a follow-up email is meant to thank the employer and show interest.
ww.A request that the employer forward your: Asking the employer to forward your resume to others is not the purpose of a follow-up email, which thanks the interviewer and restates your interest in the position.
ww.A long list of your hobbies and interest: A long list of hobbies adds clutter and is not what a follow-up email contains, since the message should thank the interviewer and remind the employer why you suit the job.

map.So they can write your resume for you an: A paid vacation that new workers receive in their first month

rw: A probationary period is an early time in a new job when the employer closely reviews performance, and it decides whether the worker is kept on after the trial ends.

ww.A paid vacation that new workers receive: A paid vacation in the first month is not what a probationary period is, which is a trial time when a new hire's performance is closely watched and reviewed by managers.
ww.A period when workers cannot be fired fo: A rule that workers cannot be fired for any reason is the opposite of probation, because a probationary period lets the employer end employment more easily if the new hire performs poorly.
ww.The final week of employment after a wor: The final week before leaving a job is a notice period, not probation, which comes at the start of employment and tests whether the new employee suits the job.

map.Skip learning about the job or the firm: A license that lets an adult drive a car on public roads
map.A ticket to a work event: A pass that gets a worker into a company event for free
map.Memorize only one answer and use it for: A form employers use to report a worker's yearly wages

rt: An official document that allows a minor to work legally
rw: A work permit is an official document that lets a minor work legally, so employers can check that the young worker's age, hours and duties follow child labor rules.

ww.A license that lets an adult drive a car: A driving license lets an adult drive on public roads and has nothing to do with legal employment of young workers, so it cannot be what a work permit is.
ww.A pass that gets a worker into a company: A pass that gets a worker into a company event is only a ticket for entry and does not give a minor legal permission to hold a paid job.
ww.A form employers use to report a worker': A form that reports yearly wages is a W-2, which employers issue after work is done; it is not the permit that allows a minor to start working legally.

map.Arriving late with an excuse ready: To cut the pay of young workers
map.To ban all teen jobs: To stop teens from ever working
map.Interrupting the interviewer often: To help firms avoid paying any taxes

rt: To protect young workers from harm
rw: Employers must follow child labor laws because the laws protect young workers from harm, setting limits on hours, hazardous tasks and school conflicts so teens stay safe, healthy and in school.

ww.To cut the pay of young workers: Child labor laws do not exist to cut young workers' pay; they set minimum ages, limit hours and protect teens, and cutting wages would run against that purpose of the laws.
ww.To stop teens from ever working: Child labor laws do not ban all teen jobs, since teens may work within limits on hours and tasks; the laws regulate work and do not forbid it completely.
ww.To help firms avoid paying any taxes: Child labor laws do not help firms avoid taxes; they protect minors, and employers who ignore them face fines, penalties or legal action from the government.

map.Post interview details online: A form to request a day off

rt: A form for tax withholding
rw: The W-4 tells an employer how much federal income tax to withhold from each paycheck, which is why new employees complete it when they start a job and sometimes update it later.

ww.A form reporting yearly wages: Yearly wages reported to the worker and the government appear on the W-2, not the W-4, which only tells an employer how much tax to hold back from pay.
ww.A form for applying to a job: A job application is a separate form that applicants fill out to be considered for hiring, whereas the W-4 is completed after being hired to set tax withholding.
ww.A form to request a day off: Asking for a day off is done with a leave request, not a W-4, which is a tax form given to new employees at the start of a job.

map.Your entire life story, starting from ch: A form telling the employer how much tax to withhold each pay
map.I do not know what to say about myself t: A form that a worker fills out to apply for a job opening
map.A form for job applications: A form that proves a minor may legally take a job at a firm

rt: A yearly form from an employer reporting wages and taxes withheld
rw: The W-2 is a yearly form from an employer reporting a worker's wages and the taxes withheld, which the worker needs to file a tax return each year.

ww.A form telling the employer how much tax: Telling employers how much tax to withhold is the job of the W-4, which a worker completes when starting a job; the W-2 reports what happened after the year ends.
ww.A form that a worker fills out to apply: Applying for a job uses an application form or resume, not the W-2, which a worker only receives after earning wages from an employer during a tax year.
ww.A form that proves a minor may legally t: Proof that a minor may work legally is a work permit, not a W-2; the W-2 reports earnings and taxes after the worker has been paid for the year.

map.Waiting for employers to call, since the: Supply, demand, price and quantity of goods
map.Connecting computers at work through a w: Taxes, tariffs, quotas and subsidies on trade

rt: Land, labor, capital and entrepreneurship
rw: The factors of production are land, labor, capital and entrepreneurship, the four inputs an economy combines to make goods and services, so this list names exactly what the question asks.

ww.Supply, demand, price and quantity of go: Supply, demand, price and quantity describe how markets work and do not name the inputs used to make goods and services, so they cannot be the factors of production.
ww.Buyers, sellers, banks and brokers in a: Buyers, sellers, banks and brokers are participants in a market and not the inputs used to produce goods, so they are not the factors of production.
ww.Taxes, tariffs, quotas and subsidies on: Taxes, tariffs, quotas and subsidies are government policies on trade, and none of them is an input used to make goods, so they are not factors of production.

rw: A factory building and its machines are man-made goods used to produce other goods, which economists call capital, so capital is the factor these items represent.

ww.Land: Land means natural resources such as soil, water and minerals, and a factory with its machines is man-made, so it is not land.
ww.Labor: Labor is the work done by people, and buildings and machines are not people, so a factory and its equipment cannot count as labor in this sense.
ww.Profit: Profit is the money left after costs, not a factor of production, so it cannot describe a building and machines used to make goods and services.

map.The law of demand: The law of demand: higher prices lower the amount bought
map.Name a weakness that makes you unfit for: The law of diminishing returns in a factory's output
map.Say you have no weaknesses at all in any: The law of comparative advantage in international trade

rt: The law of supply: higher prices bring more goods offered
rw: The law of supply says that when price rises, sellers offer more for sale, which matches concert tickets getting costlier while more of them are offered for sale.

ww.The law of demand: higher prices lower t: The law of demand says buyers purchase less as price rises, but this question describes sellers offering more at a higher price, so demand does not fit.
ww.The law of diminishing returns in a fact: Diminishing returns describes how extra inputs add less output in a factory, which has nothing to do with sellers offering more tickets when the price goes up.
ww.The law of comparative advantage in inte: Comparative advantage explains why countries trade based on lower opportunity costs, and it does not describe sellers offering more tickets when prices rise, so it does not apply.

rt: It rises, as buyers switch from costly coffee to tea
rw: When coffee gets much costlier, buyers switch to tea as a substitute, so demand for tea rises; that shift shows how substitutes respond when a related price goes up.

map.It stays the same: It stays the same, as tea and coffee are unrelated
map.A rejection letter sent to an applicant: It falls, because tea and coffee are used together
map.A request from you to leave a job, hande: It drops to zero because all buyers stop drinking tea

ww.It stays the same, as tea and coffee are: Tea and coffee are substitutes, so a price jump in one does affect the other; saying demand stays the same ignores that buyers move toward the cheaper drink.
ww.It falls, because tea and coffee are use: Demand for tea would fall only if tea and coffee were complements, but they are substitutes, so buyers who leave coffee will buy tea and raise its demand.
ww.It drops to zero because all buyers stop: Demand for tea would not drop to zero, because many people still enjoy tea and some will buy more of it when coffee becomes too costly for them.

map.Nothing, as all offers are the same: An economy where custom and tradition decide what is made and who gets it
map.Only the color of the office walls: An economy with no trade at all, where each home makes only what it uses

rw: In a market economy, individuals and businesses make most decisions through markets, using prices and competition to decide what is produced and who receives it, with limited government involvement.

ww.An economy where the government decides: Having the government decide everything describes a command economy, not a market economy, where individuals and businesses decide and the market, not the state, answers what is produced and who gets it.
ww.An economy where custom and tradition de: Custom and tradition deciding what is made describes a traditional economy, not a market economy, where individuals and businesses make most decisions through markets, prices and competition.
ww.An economy with no trade at all, where e: An economy with no trade at all, where each home makes only what it uses, is a subsistence economy and not a market economy that depends on exchange.

map.A message firing you from the job that y: A market economy driven by prices and competition
map.Market economy: A command economy planned by the government
map.A message offering you a job, sent after: A mixed economy with equal state and private roles

rt: A traditional economy based on custom and habit
rw: A village where farmers grow what their parents grew and trade by custom has a traditional economy, where habit and inherited roles decide what is made, how and for whom.

ww.A market economy driven by prices and co: A market economy relies on prices and competition rather than custom, so it does not match a village where farmers follow what their parents grew and trade by long-standing habit.
ww.A command economy planned by the governm: A command economy uses central planning by the government, but the village in the question follows custom and not state orders, so command does not describe it.
ww.A mixed economy with equal state and pri: A mixed economy blends state and private decisions, whereas the village follows custom and heritage alone, with neither markets nor the state doing much to direct production.

rw: The profit motive is the desire to earn money, which drives businesses to produce goods and services that buyers want and to lower their costs to keep more profit.

map.Inflation of prices: A law that sets the highest prices firms may charge
map.A law about prices: A tax that the state charges on the earnings of firms
map.A tax on profits: The general rise in prices of goods over a long time

ww.A law that sets the highest prices firms: A law that sets the highest price firms may charge is a price ceiling, which limits profit and is not the desire to earn money that drives production.
ww.A tax that the state charges on the earn: A tax on earnings is a government charge that takes part of profit away, and it is not the desire for profit that motivates a business owner.
ww.The general rise in prices of goods over: A general rise in prices over time is inflation, which is a measure of price change and not the desire to earn money that drives firms.

rt: A nonprofit
rw: A nonprofit works for a public purpose and uses its income for that cause instead of paying owners, which matches a group that spends all bake sale proceeds on a shelter.

ww.A franchise: A franchise is a business that licenses a brand to owners who operate for profit, so it does not fit a group that gives all proceeds to a shelter.
ww.A retail chain: A retail chain is a for-profit set of stores that keeps profit for its owners, so it is unlike a group sending all proceeds to a shelter.
ww.A monopoly: A monopoly is a single seller with no competitors who often charges high prices for profit, which is the opposite of a group donating all its proceeds.

rw: The three main activities of a business are production, marketing and finance: making goods and services, selling them to customers, and managing money so the firm can operate and grow.

ww.Reading, writing and mathematics: Reading, writing and mathematics are school subjects and do not describe the activities a business carries out, so this list cannot name the three main types of business activities.
ww.Planning, taxing and borrowing: Planning, taxing and borrowing mix general management tasks and a government action, so they are not the standard three activities that every business carries out to operate.
ww.Eating, sleeping and relaxing daily: Eating, sleeping and relaxing are personal daily habits and not business activities, so they cannot be the three main activities that a business carries out.

map.A bakery that sells bread only overall: A bakery that sells bread and cakes
map.A farm growing wheat: A farm that grows wheat for sale
map.A car factory: A factory that builds cars daily

rt: A salon that cuts and styles hair
rw: A salon that cuts and styles hair sells work performed for customers and not a physical product, which is what makes it a service business.

ww.A bakery that sells bread and cakes: A bakery sells bread and cakes, which are physical goods it bakes and sells, so it is a product business and not a service business.
ww.A farm that grows wheat for sale: A farm that grows wheat for sale produces a physical good, wheat, so it is a producer of goods and not a service business.
ww.A factory that builds cars daily: A factory that builds cars makes a physical good from raw materials, so it is a manufacturer and not a service business that sells work or expertise.

map.A product sold at a discount price: A firm that makes goods in a factory
map.A business that makes products from raw: A firm that sells only skilled services
map.A product that replaces another one: A firm that gives away goods for free

rt: A firm that buys goods to resell them
rw: A merchandising business buys finished goods from suppliers and resells them to customers at a higher price, which is how stores earn their profit without manufacturing the items.

ww.A firm that makes goods in a factory: A firm that makes goods from raw materials in a factory is a manufacturer, which creates products and does not simply resell finished goods like a merchandising business.
ww.A firm that sells only skilled services: A firm that sells only skilled services is a service business, since it offers work for others, and it does not buy finished goods to resell.
ww.A firm that gives away goods for free: A firm that gives away goods for free would have no sales income, so it cannot be a merchandising business, which earns money by reselling goods.

rw: Entrepreneurs start and run new ventures, so they must be willing to take calculated risks, weighing possible gains and losses before acting, and this trait is the most important to success.

map.It stays the same in price and in sales: Fear of every change in the market
map.It becomes impossible to measure at all: Refusal to ever learn from mistakes
map.Avoiding every decision: Waiting for others to make all decisions

ww.Fear of every change in the market: Fear of every change would stop an entrepreneur from adapting to the market, so it is a weakness and not the most important trait.
ww.Refusal to ever learn from mistakes: Refusing to learn from mistakes keeps a business from improving, so it is a poor trait, whereas entrepreneurs need to adjust after setbacks to survive.
ww.Waiting for others to make all decisions: Waiting for others to make all decisions is the opposite of entrepreneurship, which needs someone to take charge, decide and accept the risk of new ventures.

rw: Profit equals revenue minus expenses, so $12,000 - $9,500 = $2,500, which is the amount the shop earns after paying all its costs.

ww.$21,500: Adding expenses to revenue gives $21,500 ($12,000 + $9,500), but profit is found by subtracting expenses from revenue, so this uses the wrong operation.
ww.$9,500: The amount of $9,500 is only the shop's expenses and ignores the $12,000 it earned, so it reports costs and not profit.
ww.$12,000: The amount of $12,000 is revenue before any costs are paid, so it ignores the $9,500 of expenses that must be subtracted to find profit.

rw: Each unit contributes $10 - $6 = $4 toward fixed costs, so break-even is $1,000 / $4 = 250 units, the point where total revenue equals total costs.

ww.167 units: The result of 167 units comes from $1,000 divided by $6, which uses the variable cost and ignores that each sale contributes the $4 difference between price and variable cost.
ww.1,000 units: The amount of 1,000 units simply repeats the fixed cost figure in dollars, and break-even quantity needs $1,000 divided by the $4 contribution per unit.
ww.100 units: The figure of 100 units comes from $1,000 divided by $10, which uses the price alone and ignores that $6 of every sale goes to variable costs.

rw: Net profit before taxes is sales minus COGS minus operating expenses, so $50,000 - $30,000 - $12,000 = $8,000, which is what remains after paying both the product cost and running costs.

ww.$92,000: Adding all three figures gives $92,000 ($50,000 + $30,000 + $12,000), but costs must be subtracted from sales, so this adds when it should subtract.
ww.$18,000: The amount of $18,000 does not come from the required subtraction; it only subtracts $12,000 from $30,000 of COGS, which mixes up the roles of sales and costs.
ww.$20,000: The amount of $20,000 is gross profit ($50,000 - $30,000), which leaves out the $12,000 of operating expenses that must also be subtracted to reach net profit.

rt: An amount added to the cost price
rw: A markup is an amount added to the cost of an item to set its selling price, so the seller covers expenses and earns a profit.

map.Getting both choices free at no cost: A fall in price caused by a sale
map.A tax on goods: A tax charged on goods at sale

ww.A fall in price caused by a sale: A fall in price during a sale is a markdown, which is the opposite of a markup because it lowers the price instead of adding to cost.
ww.A swap of money between two banks: A swap of money between two banks is an interbank transfer and has nothing to do with how a store sets prices above its cost.
ww.A tax charged on goods at sale: A tax charged on goods at sale is a sales tax paid to the government and not an amount the seller adds to cost to set a price.

rw: A 50% markup on $20 is $10, and adding it to the cost gives $20 + $10 = $30, the selling price of the item.

ww.$70: The figure of $70 adds the 50 from the percentage as dollars to the $20 cost, but a 50% markup is half of the cost, not $50.
ww.$10: The figure of $10 is only the markup amount (50% of $20), and the selling price must add that markup to the $20 cost.
ww.$40: The figure of $40 doubles the cost, which would be a 100% markup, but a 50% markup adds only half the $20 cost, giving $30.

map.A fall in the number of workers over yea: A sole proprietorship run by one person
map.A rise in the size of a store or a shop: A general partnership with shared debts
map.A garage sale: A joint business with unlimited liability

rt: A limited liability company or corporation
rw: A limited liability company or corporation is a separate legal entity, so owners are generally not personally responsible for business debts, which protects their personal assets.

ww.A sole proprietorship run by one person: A sole proprietorship has one owner who is personally responsible for business debts, so personal assets are not protected, and it fails the requirement in this question.
ww.A general partnership with shared debts: A general partnership shares debts among partners, and each partner can be personally liable for them, so personal assets remain at risk and it does not protect owners.
ww.A joint business with unlimited liabilit: A joint business with unlimited liability leaves owners personally responsible for what the firm owes, so it is the opposite of a form that protects personal assets.

map.The path a product takes to a customer f: The financial plan, which lists costs and income forecasts
map.Employee handbook: The operations plan, which describes how work gets done
map.A bike route in a city that riders use t: The company description, which gives its history and goals

rt: The marketing plan, which describes promotion and sales
rw: The marketing plan explains how the company will attract customers through promotion, pricing, products and distribution, so it is the business plan section that answers this question.

ww.The financial plan, which lists costs an: The financial plan covers costs, income forecasts and funding, and it does not explain how the company will attract customers, which is the work of the marketing plan.
ww.The operations plan, which describes how: The operations plan describes how the company will do its daily work, with locations, equipment and suppliers, and it does not explain how to attract customers.
ww.The company description, which gives its: The company description gives the history, goals and structure of the business, and it does not set out how the company will attract customers.

map.Businesses stop producing goods here: A tax on the profit a business earns
map.Prices are fixed by law for all goods: A loan to help a new business start
map.A customer review: A written plan for a new business

rt: Legal permission to run a business
rw: A license is legal permission from a government to run a business or trade, which shows the firm meets the rules set for its field or location.

ww.A tax on the profit a business earns: Legal permission to run a business is a license, not a tax on the profit a business earns; a profit tax is paid after income is earned.
ww.A loan to help a new business start: A loan is borrowed money that a firm must repay, and it is not the legal permission that a license gives to run a business.
ww.A written plan for a new business: A written plan for a new business is a business plan, which describes goals and finances, and it does not give government permission to operate as a license does.
